angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 327,814 km at 3.29 pc = 1.33 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 304.1354 +/- 0.0200 mas (same row, RUWE 0.93): 3.29 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.4712 +/- 0.0086 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 887: radius in solar radii, 0.4712 +/- 0.0086, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112): 327,814 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.522 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 887: mass 0.522 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3676 +/- 35 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 887: effective temperature in K, 3676 +/- 35, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 887: effective temperature in K, 3676 +/- 35, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/lacaille-9352.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.809, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 887 (pscomppars): spectral type M1 V, from Hartogh et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A..93H/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 887 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.06 dex, from Hartogh et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A..93H/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 887 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.43415, from Hartogh et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A..93H/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 887 (pscomppars): age 2.9 Gyr, from Hartogh et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A..93H/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 887 (pscomppars): rotation period 38.7 d, from Hartogh et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A..93H/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 887 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 2.5 km/s, from Hartogh et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A..93H/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
